target-heart-rate-calculator.assumptionNote: 220 - age estimates max HR; individual max varies. Not for heart patients without medical guidance.
benefits: Stops the 'am I working hard enough?' guessing.
Personalized by your resting HR - fitter hearts get fairer zones.
Keeps easy days easy and hard days hard.
Explains the famous zones simply, with your numbers.

faqs.a: 60-100 bpm is the normal range; trained athletes often sit at 40-60. Lower generally means a fitter heart - unless it comes with dizziness, which needs a doctor.
faqs.q: What is a good resting heart rate?

faqs.a: Plain % of max ignores fitness. Two 30-year-olds share max 190, but with resting 50 vs 80 their aerobic zones differ hugely. Karvonen's reserve accounts for that.
faqs.q: Why Karvonen instead of plain percentages of max?

faqs.a: The 60-70% 'fat burn' zone uses the highest fat percentage - but higher zones burn more total calories and thus more total fat. For fat loss, total calories matter more than the zone name.
faqs.q: Which zone burns the most fat?

faqs.a: A graded exercise test in a lab is the gold standard. A field test (hard 3-minute hill effort, take the peak) gets close. Never max out alone or without warm-up.
faqs.q: How do I find my true max HR?

faqs.a: Watches often use % of max, not Karvonen, and estimate max from age. If your resting HR is low, Karvonen zones (like these) fit you better.
faqs.q: My watch zones differ - which is right?

faqs.a: Lightly. Start with perceived effort (can you talk?) and add zones once you train regularly. Zones shine for structured training, not first-month fitness.

target-heart-rate-calculator.formula:
Max HR = 220 - age
HRR = max HR - resting HR
Target = resting HR + HRR x intensity

Example: age 30, resting 60
Max = 220 - 30 = 190; HRR = 190 - 60 = 130
Aerobic 70-80%: 60 + 130 x 0.70 = 151 to 60 + 130 x 0.80 = 164 bpm
howTo: Enter your resting heart rate (morning, at rest).
Your max HR, reserve, and all five zones appear instantly.
Pick the zone matching your workout goal.
Recheck yearly - max HR falls about 1 beat per year with age.
keyFacts: Max HR is about 220 - age (estimate; fitter people often exceed it).
Heart-rate reserve (HRR) = max HR - resting HR.
Karvonen: target = resting + HRR x intensity.
Zones: 50-60% warm-up, 60-70% fat burn, 70-80% aerobic, 80-90% anaerobic, 90-100% max.
Measure resting HR first thing in the morning, before coffee.
Beta-blockers and some medicines blunt heart rate - zones do not apply the same way.

target-heart-rate-calculator.quickAnswer: Max heart rate is about 220 minus age; the Karvonen formula then scales training zones to your heart-rate reserve. At 30 with a resting 60, max is 190 and reserve is 130 - so the aerobic zone (70-80%) is 151-164 bpm. Five zones from 50% to 100% are listed below.
target-heart-rate-calculator.tagline: Find your exercise heart-rate zones with the Karvonen formula.
target-heart-rate-calculator.workedExample:
Age 30, resting heart rate 60 bpm:
1. Max HR: 220 - 30 = 190 bpm.
2. HRR: 190 - 60 = 130 bpm.
3. Warm-up 50-60%: 60 + 65 = 125 to 60 + 78 = 138 bpm.
4. Fat burn 60-70%: 138 to 151 bpm.
5. Aerobic 70-80%: 151 to 164 bpm.
6. Anaerobic 80-90%: 164 to 177 bpm.
7. Max 90-100%: 177 to 190 bpm.
